name: Bridge Pose
hero_alt: Bridge Pose, seen from the side
meta_description: Hips not lifting, low back doing the work, chin pressed into your chest? Three things usually hold back Bridge Pose, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
og_description: Three things usually hold back Bridge Pose, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
lede: Hips lifted by your glutes, knees over your ankles, neck resting neutral. Here’s the rubric Posewise measures it against, and what to train when you miss.
rubric_intro: Posewise checks four things from the side. Here’s what good looks like.

rubric.name: Low back
rubric.good: Lift from your glutes, not an arch in your low back

fixes.why: The shape is there, the height isn’t. That points to glute and hamstring strength, not technique.
fixes.cue: Press through your feet and lift your hips a little higher.

fixes.outcome: your lift will come from your glutes instead of your low back.
fixes.why: When the glutes don’t do the lifting, the low back usually arches to make up the height.
fixes.cue: Squeeze your glutes and press evenly through your feet.

fixes.outcome: it will stay long and safe under load.
fixes.why: Your neck bears weight in Bridge. A chin jammed into the chest, or a head pressing back, puts that load in the wrong place.
fixes.cue: Let your head rest heavy and keep your chin off your chest.

cues: And one cue: walk your feet close enough to your hips that your knees stack over your ankles.

faq.q: How high should my hips go in Bridge Pose?
faq.a: Aim for your thighs to be about parallel to the floor, but only as high as your glutes can lift you without a pinch in your low back.

faq.q: Where should my feet be in Bridge Pose?
faq.a: Hip-width apart and parallel, close enough that your fingertips can graze your heels, so your shins are close to vertical.

faq.q: Can I turn my head in Bridge Pose?
faq.a: No. Your neck is bearing weight, so keep your head still and your gaze straight up. Turn it only after you lower down.

faq.q: Why do my knees splay out in Bridge Pose?
faq.a: Usually from clenching the glutes too hard. Firm them just enough to lift, and keep your knees pointing straight ahead over your feet.

faq.q: How can I check my Bridge Pose form at home?
faq.a: Film yourself from the side. Or use Posewise, an iPhone app that measures your Bridge Pose with the camera, speaks corrections as you hold it, and builds a six-minute daily plan for what it finds.

llms_summary: the three things that usually hold back Bridge Pose (glute and hamstring strength for hip height, core control so the low back doesn’t do the lifting, a neutral neck under load), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
